name: Infinity Infoway Limited
sector: Enterprise software implementation, support and examination technology
identity_note: BSE 544567. The NSE interoperable INFINITY$ alias is not evidence of an NSE listing. Former private company; German subsidiary dissolved in 2021.
summary: Infinity Infoway is a growing ERP implementation and support business with emerging examination-security and AI products, not yet an evidence-backed recurring-software compounder. FY26 revenue reached ₹23.77 crore, but CFO was only ₹2.92 crore against ₹9.99 crore cash capex, and development assets rose to ₹8.16 crore. The decisive hold is a traced but unresolved ₹0.5639 crore annual cash-flow reconciliation, compounded by unverified current funding and product/cohort returns. At the secondary ₹599.85 close on 19 October 2026, market value is ₹327.10 crore and TTM P/E about 41.0×. Ordinary returns and entry prices remain null. material_facts: Repeated filing and control exceptions; nonoperating and related-party loans require monitoring.
Unmodified statutory audit; June promoter ownership 68.49%, no disclosed pledge.
factor_audit.contrary_fact: Management describes regularized filings, no exercised FY26 options and a May 2026 internal-auditor appointment. No established diversion.
factor_audit.rationale: Mixed stewardship and controls: historical compliance errors, related-party advances and remedial actions need verification. There is no substantiated severe minority abuse in the reviewed evidence.

material_facts: Embedded ERP workflows and domain knowledge may create switching friction.
No audited retention, pricing-power, market-share or cohort-return proof; regional concentration remains high.
factor_audit.contrary_fact: Actual deployments and a granted patent demonstrate capability, not necessarily durable economic rents.
factor_audit.rationale: Moderate niche expertise and switching friction, but no demonstrated network effect or durable pricing power. A patent and technology branding do not establish economic rents.

material_facts: Four-year revenue CAGR 43.05%; three-year 66.26%. FY26 service growth 58.78% supports more than hardware pass-through.
FY23 revenue declined 8.90%; the older FY22 base is retained.
factor_audit.contrary_fact: Q1FY27 growth is strong, but one quarter is not an independent trajectory bonus.
factor_audit.rationale: Starting band 9 from the three-year 66.26% CAGR because five-year history is unavailable, capped at 8 for medium confidence and limited comparable history. Four-year 43.05% is contextual, not the scoring period. No extra small-base haircut or forecast bonus.

material_facts: Education digitization, industrial ERP and the five-year Gujarat order support demand access.
Procurement, renewals and unproved paid product adoption limit certainty.
factor_audit.contrary_fact: Existing university relationships can produce repeat support and change-request revenue.
factor_audit.rationale: An accessible digitization runway exists, but retention, procurement and commercialization constrain duration. The management backlog is not audited ARR.

material_facts: Development assets ₹8.1556 crore; ZeroTouch and AI commercialization remains immature.
Project/cohort returns after maintenance R&D, SBC and working capital are not disclosed.
factor_audit.contrary_fact: Asset-light software can produce excellent incremental returns. It is not mechanically penalized.
factor_audit.rationale: NS: project or cohort cash returns, capitalization lives and full reinvestment requirements are not established. Historical book returns are not a valid substitute. No mechanical asset-light penalty.

material_facts: FY24–26 reported CFO/PAT 0.514×; FCF proxy −₹5.6933 crore.
FY26 receivables absorbed ₹3.4235 crore; over-one-year balances were ₹1.4016 crore.
factor_audit.contrary_fact: Excluding ₹1.9817 crore FY26 nonoperating loan outflow improves three-year conversion to 0.649×, still weak.
factor_audit.rationale: Persistent conversion below 0.6× on reported three-year totals, with aged receivables and a negative reinvestment cash balance. Removing FY26 nonoperating loan outflow improves the ratio to 0.649×, not to strong conversion. GQS cap 5 applies.

material_facts: Zero FY26 funded debt, but ₹17.8049 crore bank book balances are not verified current unrestricted cash.
Cash/proceeds bridges, earmarks, guarantees and development commitments constrain financing assessment.
factor_audit.contrary_fact: No actual default is evidenced; retained profits and low reported leverage are positive.
factor_audit.rationale: NS: bank and IPO-proceeds availability, cash-flow reconciliation and current obligations are not sufficiently verified. Zero reported funded debt is positive evidence, not proof of financeability.

material_facts: Core service growth and the government contract demonstrate execution.
New-product cash conversion and reporting controls remain incomplete.
factor_audit.contrary_fact: Patent grant, manufactured devices and pilots are concrete, though not commercial-return proof.
factor_audit.rationale: Core implementation and revenue execution are credible; commercial product adoption and public-company controls remain incompletely demonstrated.

material_facts: FY26 PAT ₹7.0115 crore; June TTM PAT ₹7.9844 crore.
Development additions ₹8.1461 crore and rising amortization make normalization important.
factor_audit.contrary_fact: Revenue growth is genuine and other income is separately identified. The audit is unmodified.
factor_audit.rationale: Reported profit growth is meaningful, but development capitalization, amortization timing and cash conversion limit confidence in normalized owner earnings.

material_facts: Ordinary returns and entry prices are null while current funding and reliability remain unresolved.
Base conditional return is about 3.02%, not a supported ordinary return input.
factor_audit.contrary_fact: Bull conditional return is about 20.81%, but requires optimistic linked assumptions.
factor_audit.rationale: NS: a conditional model on unverified funds cannot supply a supported return factor. Ordinary returns and entry prices remain null.

Opening cash-floor breach appears under FD-availability and collection stress.
factor_audit.contrary_fact: Reported CFO is positive and funded debt is zero; no imminent default is asserted.
factor_audit.rationale: Score 3 measures conditional price-impairment severity and sensitivity, not an asserted probability of rescue or actual default. The bear diagnostic loses about 75% of terminal per-share value; funding-availability stress breaches the opening cash floor. Actual financing resilience remains BAL NS.

material_facts: 15% hurdle at 15× terminal EBIT and 33% EBIT margin requires roughly ₹127.71 crore annualized terminal revenue.
The historical-anchor-to-terminal span is 5.555 years, distinct from the five-year investor horizon.
factor_audit.contrary_fact: Historical growth is higher, but its small base, uncertain retention and reinvestment need qualification.
factor_audit.rationale: Several optimistic growth, margin, reinvestment and exit assumptions must hold together to reach the hurdle; price-implied expectations leave limited room for error.

Only 20 secondary sessions are available; official 60-session history, spread and current restrictions are missing.

factor_audit.rationale: NS: incomplete secondary history and unverified spread/restrictions cannot establish executable liquidity. Missing observations are not zero-volume sessions.

sections.title: Research Header, Gates and Data Confidence
sections.text:
Infinity Infoway Limited, formerly Infinity Infoway Private Limited, is BSE SME security 544567, ISIN INE16XA01017. It listed on 8 October 2025. The company’s dissolved German subsidiary is not an active operating subsidiary. The working financial scope is consolidated Ind AS, including equity-method treatment of Infinity Transoft, not a wholly owned group perimeter. [S1,S4,S6,S9]

Information cutoff: 20 October 2026. The secondary historical BSE close on 19 October is ₹599.85, independently corroborated by another secondary quote. On 5,453,000 issued shares, market capitalization is ₹327.0982 crore. The official interoperable security master confirms a 400-share lot. Its INFINITY$ / SM alias does not establish a separate NSE listing. The five-year investor horizon is 20 October 2026 to 20 October 2031, with a 15% nominal, pre-investor-tax equity hurdle and an illustrative ₹5 lakh position. This is not an allocation recommendation. [M1–M3]

G1 is Conditional; G2 and G3 are Hold — unresolved; G4 is Conditional. Identity and exact source arithmetic have high confidence. Reported financial history, growth composition and governance have medium confidence. Current available cash, attributable incremental returns and ordinary investment valuation have low confidence. Overall investment confidence is low rather than an average that hides those gaps. Results released after the cutoff, including any September 2026 result, are excluded.

sections.title: Scorecard and Calculation Audit
sections.text:
Canonical factors: GOV 5, MOAT 5, REV 8, DUR 6, CAP NS, CASH 3, BAL NS, EXEC 6, EARN 5, R NS, D 3, P 3 and L NS. BQS, GQS and IAS remain NS. GQS means Growth Quality Score; IAS factor P means price-implied expectations. The exact Decimal calculations below preserve the framework weights and do not redistribute missing weights.

BQS has known weighted contribution 4.34 and 80% coverage; its missing-data bound is 4.54–6.34. GQS has known contribution 5.45 and 85% coverage; the raw bound is 5.60–6.95. Persistent CASH 3 applies the stated GQS cap of 5 to any computable score, but does not replace NS with 5. IAS has known contribution 0.90 and 30% coverage; its bound is 1.60–7.90. These are mathematical bounds, not confidence intervals, midpoint estimates or rankable scores.

EARN enters GQS, not BQS. BQS enters IAS once. Changing GOV or MOAT by one point changes the BQS known contribution by 0.20, but cannot close CAP/BAL gaps. All three ranking flags are false. The framework is a research policy heuristic, not a statistically validated predictor of return or fraud. [E02–E19]

sections.title: Business Overview
sections.text:
Infinity provides customized ERP software to education and industrial customers, implementation, annual support/subscriptions, changes and upgrades, examination services and small digital-marketing services. These are economically different activities. The disclosures do not provide audited ARR, gross retention, net revenue retention, subscription-only margins or customer-cohort payback. Long contracts and embedded workflows support a plausible renewal mechanism, but customers are not obliged to renew. [S1,S7]

FY26 service revenue was ₹20.9467 crore, 88.12% of total sales. Software implementation/support contributed ₹18.5330 crore, examination services ₹2.3827 crore and digital marketing ₹0.0310 crore. New hardware revenue of ₹2.8236 crore was matched by ₹2.7798 crore purchase cost, leaving just ₹0.0438 crore gross spread before overhead. Hardware volume is therefore not equivalent to high-margin recurring software growth. [S4]

The FY25 prospectus identified 38 material university agreements: 29 government and nine private. Collections depend on procurement, implementation acceptance and institutional payment processes. Tender deposits, bank guarantees and security requirements are part of the cash model. ZeroTouch proposes a device-as-a-service/per-question-paper model, not simply machine sales. The business is best analyzed as a software and implementation-services hybrid with emerging product optionality, not presumed pure SaaS.

sections.title: Moat / Industry Position
sections.text:
The plausible competitive advantages are domain knowledge, integration with university records, client-specific workflows and switching/retraining costs. The evidence is weaker for pricing power, sustained retention, market share or a network effect. FY25’s largest customer contributed 22.97% of revenue, the top five 48.51% and top ten 63.44%; Gujarat contributed 93.16%. Tender-linked revenue declined to 32.82% from 61.34% in FY24 and 65.45% in FY23, but procurement and government-budget dependence did not disappear. [S1]

Microsoft Azure and CtrlS hosting create infrastructure dependencies. Dedicated-server expense was ₹1.2805 crore in FY26 versus ₹0.8494 crore in FY25. Management describes its AI algorithms as built over an open-source model rather than paid third-party APIs. That does not establish independent model licensing, security, uptime or inference-cost performance. The granted ZeroTouch patent proves a legal grant, not monetization, customer retention or immunity from security failures. [S1,S4,S7,S12]

Three historical economic comparators are Ramco Systems for enterprise products and implementation, Ksolves for specialized service delivery, and SoftTech Engineers for government software/project economics. Ramco’s FY25 consolidated sales were ₹591.342 crore, owner-attributable loss ₹34.248 crore and CFO ₹113.347 crore: software IP does not guarantee owner profitability. Ksolves reported ₹137.4331 crore consolidated sales and 53% top-ten customer concentration. SoftTech’s FY25 presentation distinguishes 8% SaaS revenue from 24% SaaS plus transactions, rather than labeling all services recurring. These FY25 comparisons are not current valuation multiples or investment recommendations. SoftTech’s cover has an inconsistent year reference, so only its stated historical FY25 figures are used. [P1–P3]

sections.title: Revenue Growth & Scale
sections.text:
Revenue observations are FY22 ₹5.6769 crore, FY23 ₹5.1717 crore, FY24 ₹10.1716 crore, FY25 ₹13.1923 crore and FY26 ₹23.7703 crore. Annual additions were −₹0.5052, +₹4.9999, +₹3.0207 and +₹10.5780 crore. The four-year CAGR is 43.05%; the three-year CAGR is 66.26%, but starts from the depressed FY23 base. Five-year CAGR is ND without FY21, and ten-year CAGR is also ND. Five observed annual numbers do not constitute a five-year CAGR. [S1,S2,S4]

FY26 sales growth was 80.18%. Hardware explains ₹2.8236 crore of the increase, but service revenue still grew 58.78%, so growth is not solely pass-through sales. An audited price/volume/acquisition bridge was not located, and nominal revenue growth is not automatically unit-volume growth. Q1FY27 sales of ₹6.8993 crore were 119.31% above the comparable ₹3.1459 crore. TTM revenue to June 2026 is ₹27.5237 crore, calculated as FY26 plus June 2026 quarter minus June 2025 quarter. The quarter is not annualized. [S4,S6]

REV starts in band 9 from the three-year 66.26% growth rate, as prescribed when five-year history is unavailable but is capped at 8 for medium confidence and limited comparable history. No single-quarter trajectory bonus or new-product TAM bonus is applied. Using the older FY22 anchor reveals the weak FY23 base; no second mechanical small-company penalty is added.

sections.title: Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
sections.text:
Scaling requires more institutions and modules, adequate implementation/support capacity and renewals, followed by paid adoption of ZeroTouch and AI products. The disclosed ₹10.974 crore Knowledge Consortium of Gujarat contract spans five years, includes tax, and covers development, implementation, testing, operations and maintenance. It is neither annual revenue nor audited ARR. Management’s approximately ₹75 crore ERP order book as of 30 May 2026 spans around two years and includes longer contracts; a contract-level recognition, cancellation and collection bridge was not independently verified. [S7,S11]

On the 13 August call, management said 150 ZeroTouch machines had been developed, but commercial activity remained pilots and tenders without confirmed commercial orders. FY27 aspirations of ₹5–6 crore orders and eventual 55–60% EBITDA margins are management expectations, not achieved economics. AI beta and monetization milestones were also prospective. [S7]

FY26 development assets were ₹8.1556 crore, including ZeroTouch ₹4.8977 crore and AgentAI ₹0.9367 crore. Other education, industrial ERP and examination projects make up the balance. Revenue, maintenance R&D, working capital, unit contribution and payback attributable to each cohort are not available. CAP stays NS because the relevant return evidence is missing, not because software is asset-light. High book ROCE would not close this gap. Cash conversion and development commitments constrain Growth Quality; CASH 3 invokes a cap of 5, but missing CAP leaves GQS NS. [S4]

sections.title: Management, Governance & Execution
sections.text:
Management has delivered substantial core ERP/services growth and a material government contract. Patent grant on 28 April 2026, manufactured ZeroTouch devices and pilot activity are real milestones. They are not yet paid installed-base, recurring-revenue or cash-payback evidence. [S4,S7,S11,S12]

FY26 secretarial audit identified late MGT-14 filing, no timely internal-auditor appointment and post-listing ESOP grants without prior shareholder ratification. Management says late forms were filed with additional fees, no options vested/exercised/allotted during FY26, and the internal auditor was appointed on 4 May 2026. Historical prospectus disclosures also describe inconsistent German-subsidiary reporting and the wrong FY20 accounts attachment. The company states that filings were regularized and no adjudication notice had been received at the prospectus date. Those responses are preserved; repeated control failures still warrant scrutiny. [S1,S4,S16]

The 7 August AGM proceedings list proposed ESOP ratification, RPTs and borrowing/investment authorities put to vote, then say the scrutinizer’s results would follow. Final voting evidence was not independently located. Secondary headlines saying everything was approved are not a substitute. Do not claim either definitive non-approval or completed ratification from those proceedings. [S15]

June promoter ownership was 68.49%, with no pledge disclosed. FY26 related-party Transoft income was ₹0.7443 crore and receivable ₹0.1199 crore. Closing loans were ₹0.4049 crore to related Infinity Edutech and ₹1.60 crore to nonrelated Welmica Laminates, both at 9%. Directors’ remuneration was ₹0.4046 crore. These are capital-allocation and minority-protection questions, not proof of diversion. The original ₹2.0001 crore trademark allegation is not treated as a current established liability: settlement, subsequent court orders and the company’s technology-provider defense are retained. [S1,S4,S9]

sections.title: Financial Forensics
sections.text:
FY26 operating EBIT of ₹9.0147 crore and EBITDA of ₹9.8774 crore exclude ₹0.6930 crore other income. Headline EBITDA including other income is ₹10.5704 crore and is not the same operating measure. PAT of ₹7.0115 crore produced CFO of ₹2.9173 crore and a reported FCF proxy of −₹7.0754 crore after ₹9.9927 crore cash capex. CFO starts from PBT ₹9.6478 crore and pre-working-capital cash ₹11.0783 crore; receivables absorbed ₹3.4235 crore, loans ₹1.9817 crore and cash taxes ₹2.8212 crore. Excluding nonoperating loan outflow gives an adjusted CFO diagnostic of ₹4.8990 crore, not all customer collections. Capex explains FCF pressure, not weak CFO. [S4]

FY24–26 CFO/PAT is 0.514× on a ratio-of-sums basis using restated historical PAT; original statutory PAT gives 0.507×. Removing the FY26 loan outflow lifts the restated ratio to 0.649×, still weak. Three-year FCF is −₹5.6933 crore. FY25 restated PAT ₹4.1915 crore differs from original ₹4.3834 crore because the ₹0.1919 crore prior-period tax credit was removed. Statutory and restated equity also differ; that full bridge remains open, not silently erased. Average receivable days improve from roughly 134.3 to 113.6, while balances older than one year grow from ₹0.2355 crore to ₹1.4016 crore. FY26 ECL is only ₹0.0286 crore, 0.313% of gross receivables. Improving aggregate days does not cancel ageing risk. [S1,S3,S4]

The annual cash-flow statement closes at ₹11.7017 crore, but the balance sheet and cash note show ₹11.1378 crore. The ₹0.5639 crore discrepancy equals the noncash ROU addition removed from annual investing cash flow while the closing lease balance of ₹0.5259 crore remains a financing inflow. Note 38 gives 0 + 0.5639 + 0.0320 − 0.0700 = 0.5259; lease principal paid was ₹0.0380 crore, not cash raised. The earlier May statement balances arithmetically by retaining both ROU and liability entries. Both July annual versions have identical core financial-page pixels. This traces the issue but is not an authoritative correction or proof of fraud. The May resubmission explicitly corrected only EPS and cannot be represented as resolving the later annual cash discrepancy. Audit opinions remain unmodified. [S4,S4B,S5,S16]

Net proceeds of ₹22.0086 crore versus cash share/premium proceeds ₹21.1458 crore differ by ₹0.8628 crore. Recorded issue cost ₹3.2822 crore, proceeds-estimate cost ₹2.4194 crore and prior prepaid cost ₹0.2562 crore need a cash/accrual reconciliation, without double counting. March bank book balances total ₹17.8049 crore; current unrestricted availability is ND. Unutilized IPO objects were ₹10.9159 crore in March and ₹7.4245 crore in June. Bank guarantees ₹2.6936 crore, accrued gratuity ₹0.8666 crore and leases ₹0.5259 crore are separately visible. [S4,S6,S8]

Associate accounts show FY26 equity −₹6.0167 crore, PAT ₹1.3813 crore and a ₹0.3548 crore deferred-tax credit. At 49.42%, the profit approximates the AOC-1’s ₹0.6826 crore. Accumulated deficits provide a credible unrecognized-loss/resumption explanation for no positive parent equity-method result, but the wording ‘considered in consolidation’ and cumulative-loss bridge remain unresolved. Do not invent missing earnings, control or an NCI deduction. [S3,S4,S14]

Development additions of ₹8.1461 crore are large relative to PBT. A gross expense-all-additions diagnostic leaves operating EBIT ₹0.8686 crore before a proper useful-life, tax and amortization bridge; this is not a finding that all capitalization is prohibited. Development recognition/recoverability is an audit KAM, not a qualification. FY26 statutory ROE is about 25.54% on average equity, distorted by IPO timing. Book ROCE cannot establish incremental project returns. Granted 63,710 options imply 1.168% share expansion versus 1.155% holder dilution; the full 150,000 pool implies 2.751% versus 2.677%. The pool includes the grants, and optional exercise money is not committed funding. [S4,S10]

sections.title: Valuation & Market Expectations
sections.text:
At ₹599.85 and current issued shares, the stock is 46.65× FY26 PAT, 40.97× June TTM PAT and 11.88× TTM sales. Historical weighted-share EPS ₹15.11 is not substituted into a current-share P/E. Unrestricted cash is unverified, so an ordinary EV/EBITDA point remains NS. P/E and price/sales are cross-checks, not intrinsic value. No DCF is forced on unverified retention, development returns and funding; the 15% equity hurdle is not asserted to be WACC. [S4,S6,M2]

The annual bear/base/bull model separates legacy services, hardware and new products. Initial legacy-service growth is 10%/25%/35%, fading through FY32; exit EV/EBIT multiples are 10×/15×/20×. Base EBITDA margin after cash rent and SBC rises from 35% to 38%, with 5% D&A, 1% SBC, 25.17% tax, receivables at 38% of sales, other ONWC at −2.5%, tender deposits at 6% and annual capex including development of ₹7/6/5/4/4/4 crore. These are analyst assumptions. Explicit annual cash rent is 0.5% of revenue; no lease liability is then deducted again at exit. The full option pool gives 5,603,000 claims, with no speculative exercise cash. [Model]

March IPO earmarks are tracked separately and can draw only against the same modeled eligible cash use once. Bank maturity, availability and legal eligibility remain assumptions. No cash is added from loans, gold, associate value, repeated IPO proceeds, operational property or separate IP. Required cash is max(₹2 crore, 12% of annualized revenue) plus ₹0.8666 crore opening accrued gratuity. Terminal equity includes signed free cash less required cash, not a zero-clipped surplus. [Model]

All ordinary IRRs and entry prices are null. Only on assumed cash availability and permitted earmark use do conditional bear/base/bull returns become −24.16%/+3.02%/+20.81%, with terminal per-share diagnostics ₹150.52/₹695.97/₹1,543.37. These are not executable price targets. A ₹7.4901 crore FD-availability haircut plus 60 extra collection days breaches the opening cash floor; its non-rescue return and entry fields are null. A separate counterfactual rescue at ₹300 with 3% fees raises ₹4.45377 crore gross, ₹4.32016 crore net and 148,459 new shares, causing 2.581% all-period holder dilution. The issue is pre-entry, so post-entry dilution is zero; its conditional IRR is about 1.70%. No such financing availability or legal approval is established. [Model]

At a 15% hurdle, 15× exit EBIT and 33% terminal EBIT margin, reverse expectations require about ₹127.71 crore annualized terminal revenue versus base ₹69.92 crore. The 35.34% required revenue CAGR runs from 31 March 2026 to 20 October 2031, about 5.555 years, not five. Investor holding time is exactly five calendar years. Full operating/funding stress rows and 12/15/18% hurdle sensitivities are retained. Tests vary collection delays, cash availability, margins, development spending, D&A and exit multiples. Leap-year and October stubs are explicit; post-terminal cash deficits do not contaminate the horizon. Returns exclude unquantified transaction costs and market impact.

sections.title: Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
sections.text:
The strongest bear case is not that software cannot compound. It is that a high valuation capitalizes reported profit while new-product spending is capitalized, government receivables absorb cash and current funding is not reconciled. In the linked failure path, product adoption is late, service growth slows, personnel and hosting costs persist, collections take longer and development spending continues. Asset impairment would disclose cash already consumed; subsequent dilution or curtailed R&D can permanently reduce per-share earning power. [S4,S7]

Conditional bear terminal value of ₹150.52 is about 74.91% below the reference price before trading frictions. The availability/collection stress starts below its minimum cash requirement. Later positive operating cash cannot erase an initial financing gap, so non-rescue returns remain null. Rescue is an explicitly separate counterfactual, not assumed funding. Positive reported CFO and no FY26 funded debt are important counterevidence against claiming an actual or imminent default. [Model]

The thesis-break variable is failure of paid product adoption and customer collections to replenish genuinely available funds before development commitments consume them. Permanent impairment risk is High; this is neither a probability estimate nor a statement of certain loss.

sections.title: 5× / 10× Feasibility
sections.text:
A fivefold price outcome in five years requires 37.97% annual shareholder return; tenfold requires 58.49%. At unchanged fully diluted claims and without dividends, terminal share values would need to reach ₹2,999.25 or ₹5,998.50. At 15× EBIT and a 33% EBIT margin, ignoring positive cash support, those values require roughly ₹339.5 crore or ₹679.0 crore annual revenue. This is algebra, not a market-size forecast or target. [Model]

The small operating base and new technology create optionality, but capital needs, competition, customer procurement and possible new shares must accompany any scale-up. No verified retention, cohort payback or commercial ZeroTouch order base by the cutoff supports a durable 5×/10× designation. The business is not awarded a compounder label merely because a large percentage growth rate is arithmetically possible. [S1,S4,S7]

sections.title: Monitoring Plan
sections.text:
1. Close the ₹0.5639 crore annual cash-flow discrepancy with an authoritative corrected statement and bank/lease bridge. The hold remains until reconciled.
2. Reconcile the ₹0.8628 crore IPO cost/cash difference and June ₹7.4245 crore unutilized objects with bank maturity, encumbrance and permitted use. Reject double-counted proceeds.
3. Track rolling three-year CFO/PAT: current restated-basis 0.514×. Real collection-driven recovery above 0.8× would help; continued below 0.6× is a warning.
4. Monitor ₹1.4016 crore receivables older than one year, actual recoveries and ECL adequacy, not only average days.
5. Obtain subscription/support versus implementation revenue, renewal cohorts, NRR, customer adds and concentration. Those are prerequisites for a recurring-platform thesis.
6. Validate paid ZeroTouch customers, papers processed, utilization, realized gross margins and cash payback. Devices made and pilots are not confirmed orders.
7. Reconcile ₹8.1556 crore development by project, ready-for-use dates, amortization and budgets. June-quarter D&A of ₹0.7391 crore makes useful lives especially important.
8. Verify final ESOP/RPT votes, internal-audit follow-through and related-loan recoveries.
9. Bridge associate cumulative unrecognized losses, its current profit and AOC-1 wording, without assuming parent access to associate cash.
10. Before implementation, obtain official 60-session BSE trading history, surveillance stage, spread and whole-lot depth. One 400-share lot costs ₹239,940 at the reference quote. [S4,S6–S10,S14,S15,M1–M3]

These are research triggers, not an automated trading instruction or promise to monitor future filings.

sections.title: Final Classification & Conditional Action
sections.text:
Hold — unresolved; high impairment risk. This is an established implementation business with a growth and product-commercialization thesis, not yet a verified high-quality compounder and not an evidenced default situation. BQS, GQS and IAS are NS and not ranking-eligible. Missing CAP, BAL, R and L cannot become neutral scores. [E01–E20]

The financial-reliability and current-funding holds prevent a favorable investment classification even if headline growth or the share price rises. No ordinary buy price or return is supported. An authoritative cash/proceeds/associate bridge, dated genuinely available funding and attributable development/cohort returns could change the conclusion. After that, price-sensitive valuation would need recalculation. A lower price alone does not resolve those evidence gaps. The illustrative ₹5 lakh liquidity reference is not a personal portfolio allocation, and no execution or exit is promised.

sections.title: Sources, Assumptions & Open Questions
sections.text:
Material company facts are tied to prospectuses, audited annual reports, financial results and issuer disclosures. For FY26 annual reports, direct BSE retrieval was unreliable; archived exchange-filing copies were downloaded from Business Standard, with original and mirror URLs recorded. Both July versions were compared. The very large company-hosted annual-report transfer did not complete and is not claimed as successfully retrieved. Original-byte SHA256 digests and page locators are in the source register. [S1–S16]

The 19 October price and short trading history are secondary rather than exchange-certified. Peer evidence uses dated FY25 disclosures and does not import current peer multiples. Management forecasts, analyst assumptions and calculations are labeled separately. Unavailable normalized PAT, incremental ROIC, contract assets and quarterly cash flow remain missing rather than zero. Normal consolidated-versus-standalone differences are not inherently errors. [M1–M3,P1–P3]

Open questions are the cash-flow, IPO cost, equity-restatement and associate bridges; current unrestricted cash and FD restrictions; customer payment milestones and retention; development useful lives and cohort returns; product security and unit costs; final AGM votes; and official liquidity/restrictions. These are substantive limits, not omissions hidden by a point score.

The source-free analytical archives contain safe financial extracts, calculations, source URLs/digests and reproduction code. They intentionally exclude original PDFs, OCR, HTML, images and shareholder identifiers. Reproduction verifies arithmetic and consistency, not original-source truth or fresh authentication. This research is not personalized investment advice or a trading instruction.

calculation_definitions.CFO_PAT: Sum of comparable CFO divided by sum of comparable PAT; original statutory alternative retained.
calculation_definitions.FCF: Reported CFO minus operating tangible/intangible cash capex; not automatically FCFF or FCFE. Lease and financing classifications remain separate.
calculation_definitions.EBITDA: PBT minus other income plus finance cost and D&A, unless explicitly labeled headline.
calculation_definitions.receivable_days: Average opening/closing net receivables divided by total revenue × 365; revenue is a credit-sales proxy.
calculation_definitions.cash_floor: Maximum of ₹2 crore and 12% of annualized revenue, plus ₹0.8666 crore accrued opening gratuity.
calculation_definitions.terminal_equity: Operating EV plus signed free cash less required reserves; earmarks excluded. No separate speculative IP, associate or operational-property value.
calculation_definitions.return: No interim distributions. Fifth root of terminal per-share value / entry price minus one, over exactly five calendar years. Ordinary fields remain null.
calculation_definitions.CAGR: Positive endpoints over actual year intervals; five-year CAGR requires six annual observations.

analytical_status: All numerical scenario and source-safe records embedded; ordinary investment conclusions blocked by evidence, not omitted work.
